IASC Championship on Protection from SexualExploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment
ChampionshipUpdates
The IASC Championship on Protection fromSexual Exploitation and Abuse and SexualHarassment (PSEAH) is an excellent opportunityfor WFP to lead and bolster collective efforts to create a humanitarian system free of sexualexploitation and abuse (SEA), and to strengthenour commitment to people affected by crises.
WFP Executive Director Cindy H. McCain assumed theIASC Championship at a critical moment for thehumanitarian sector. Conflict and insecurity, theaccelerating impacts of climate change, and economicshocks are driving hunger and humanitarian needsaround the world.
Hunger and displacement put more people –particularly women and children – at risk of sexualexploitation and abuse, so is more critical than ever that we ensure that people we serve receive assistancewithout risk of sexual exploitation and abuse.
Executive Director McCain has been a leading voice inthe international community, placing a spotlight oncrises around the world which require strong attentionand assistance. Her persistent advocacy for theincreased capacity to safely deliver vital assistanceattests to the importance of strong leadership acrossthe sector.
This mid-year update provides the latest information on the Executive Director’s actions andWFP’s progress toward fulfilling the three key Championship priorities:
123
Operationalizing a Victim-Survivor Centered Approach
Promoting Organizational Culture Change
Supporting Continued Capacity Strengthening Across the Sector
June 2024
As the current IASC Champion, WFP isleading on PSEAH efforts across thesector. Executive Director McCain isengaging with stakeholders at all levelsand acting as an advocate of PSEAH andensuring it remains high on the agendaacross the humanitarian sector.
Through her role and engagements,including missions to some of WFP’slargest and most complex operations,she is amplifying the voices of high-riskcommunities, and increasing awarenessand the need for collective and concreteactions to address the ongoingchallenges of implementing PSEAHacross the sector.

News and EventsJanuary through June 2024
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TAKES ON IASC PSEAH CHAMPIONSHIP
Upon taking on the Championship on31 January, WFP issued a press releaseoutlining WFP’s priorities and amplifiedthis across the Executive Director’s andcorporate social media accounts.
WFP SHARES CHAMPIONSHIPPROGRESS WITH EXTERNALSTAKEHOLDERS
The WFP Championship was launchedto the public through an onlinecampaign which included a video andposts on the IASC website. In addition,the WFP Ethics Office conductedvarious sessions with interagencygroups on WFP’s Championshippriorities. This included the IASC PSEAHTechnical Advisory Group, the UNWorking Group on SEA, theOrganisation for Economic Cooperationand Development’s DevelopmentAssistance Committee PSEAH ReferenceGroup and multiple in-country PSEANetworks. Briefings were alsoconducted for the WFP Executive Boardand to the IASC Member States.
UN HIGH-LEVEL STEERING GROUP ON PSEA
During the Meeting and Retreat of the UN High-Level Steering Group on PSEA, which wasconvened by Under-Secretary-General (USG) Christian Saunders, Special Coordinator onImproving the United Nations (UN) Response to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (OSCSEA), WFPDeputy Executive Director Carl Skau reiterated WFP’s commitment to achieve a system freefrom sexual misconduct and how WFP is using the IASC Championship to build on the extensivework done to date. He also emphasized the importance of strong leadership at all levels toeffectively implement PSEAH.
MEETING OF INVESTIGATORY BODIES ON PROTECTION FROM SEXUALEXPLOITATION, ABUSE AND SEXUALHARASSMENT (SEAH)
WFP participated in the third meeting of theinvestigatory bodies on protection from SEAHin order to strengthen discussion aroundapplying victim-centered approaches in linewith the work of the IASC Expert Panel onSEAH Investigations, which is co-chaired bythe WFP Director of the Office of Inspectionsand Investigations. The Executive Directorprovided remarks during the opening sessionto demonstrate leadership commitment toharmonized and complementary approachesto investigations into SEAH. This meeting wasorganized jointly by the IASC and the UNExecutive Group on Addressing SexualHarassment as part of their commitment toenhancing accountability, including throughtrauma-informed investigations.

EMPOWERED AID WEBINAR SERIES
WFP joined a panel as part of awebinar series hosted by EmpoweredAid. The panel featured organizationsdiscussing their efforts towardworking to reduce power disparitiesamong refugee women and girls in thehumanitarian context.
IASC PSEAH GLOBAL WORKSHOP
LEADERSHIP ENGAGEMENT
Since taking on the IASCChampionship, the Executive Directorhas engaged with leadership acrossthe IASC to lead and bolster collectiveefforts to create a humanitariansystem free from SEA and sexualharassment and strengthen ourcommitment. To mark the beginning of the Championship, the ExecutiveDirector wrote to IASC Principals tooutline the priorities for theChampionship and reiterate thatleaders share an absolute commitmentto protecting the vulnerable people weserve. The Executive Director has metwith UN leadership, including USGChristian Saunders and the (then)Victim Rights Advocate Jane Connors,to discuss her objectives for theChampionship and ways to continuestrengthening cooperation and ensurea collective accountability andstrengthened leadership across thesector. She regularly engages withpeers on the importance of this issueand the need for strong leadershipacross the UN system.
HUMANITARIAN NETWORKS ANDPARTNERSHIPS WEEK
As the PSEAH Champion, WFP chaired apanel which included experts from UNagencies, IASC and Empowered Aid andfocused on how to work together for moreeffective protections against SEAH acrossthe humanitarian sector.
The Executive Director made a special address at the second annual IASC PSEAH GlobalWorkshop in Brindisi, Italy, which was attended by PSEA Coordinators representing 30 countries,IASC experts, the Special Coordinator on Improving the UN Response to SEA, representatives ofthe UN Office of the Victims’ Rights Advocate and funding partners. The WFP Senior Advisor onPSEA also participated in a panel session focused on PSEA and partnerships.
HUMANITARIAN COORDINATOR RETREAT
At the Executive Director’s initiative, a PSEAagenda item was added to the HumanitarianCoordinators (HC) Retreat in Istanbul, Türkiye.WFP Deputy Executive Director Carl Skau ledthe session and was joined by USG ChristianSaunders. The Deputy Executive Directorhighlighted the importance of strongleadership from HCs in order to fulfil ourobligations to the people we serve, retain thesupport of our donors and partners, and tosustain the reputation of the UN as a force forgood in the world. HCs shared their ownexperiences and of their role, and sharedstrategic recommendations for strengtheningour collective work on PSEA.

Championship PrioritiesUpdates and progress
1 Operationalizing a Victim-Survivor Centered Approach
A key initiative under Priority 1 is strengtheninginformation sharing with communities on theirrights and PSEA through the “PSEA at theFrontline Phase 2” initiative.
UPDATES
Comprehensive desk research was conducted,and pilot tools and methodology weredeveloped using a human-centered designapproach to ensure that the PSEAcommunication tools respond to users’ needs.
Consultations with field staff from East Africaand Latin America were held to ensure thetools are inclusive.
Communication tools were pre-tested inselected field locations, including South Sudanand the Latin America region.
COMING SOON • Testing of methodology and tools inselected field locations, integrating human-centered design techniques.
• Consolidation of a package tocommunicate PSEA with targetcommunities.
• Translations and launch/roll-out of tools.
Another key initiative under Priority 1 is thecreation of a global advisory group consistingof women-led NGOs and civil society located inhigh-risk countries prioritized by the IASC. Theadvisory group will ensure that all aspects ofChampionship outputs apply a victim-centeredapproach relevant to local contexts.
UPDATES
Consultations were held with the IASC PSEATechnical Advisory Group, Empowered Aid,UN OVRA and OSCSEA.The Terms of Reference for the Women’sAdvisory Group were drafted and endorsedby the IASC PSEA Technical Advisory Group.The Executive Director shared a call fornominations for Advisory Group Members.
COMING SOON
The Advisory Group members will beselected.The Advisory Group will convene forits first consultation through avirtual meeting in Q3 2024.An in-person workshop for theAdvisory Group will be organized forQ4 2024.

The last key initiative under Priority 1 is strengthening interagency standards on PSEAH bypromoting the adoption of tools and resources developed in connection with the UN ExecutiveGroup to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Harassment, an initiative to support the practicalimplementation of a victim-centered approach.
UPDATES
WFP presented the Results Framework at the IASC and UN Executive Group Meeting ofInvestigatory Bodies on PSEAH in Geneva.
COMING SOON
In conjunction with the Secretariat of the UN Executive Group to Prevent and Respond to SexualHarassment (EG), WFP has selected the “Results Framework” as the main tool and resource to befurther promoted among IASC members. The Results Framework was developed under WFP’s leadand was endorsed by the EG entities in January 2024. The Framework is a set of forward-thinkingindicators of good practices for preventing and responding to sexual harassment.
The Framework is intended to support entities in achieving (i) implementation of the victim-centered approach; (ii) policy progress; (iii) system-wide consistency on sexual harassmentthrough greater collaboration and knowledge sharing; and (iv) enhanced data collection to enableregular and sustainable monitoring of efforts across the system.
WFP will formally submit the Results Framework to IASC members for their review andendorsement to drive tangible improvements in how the sector approaches prevention andresponse to sexual harassment.

2 Promoting Organizational Culture Change
A key initiative under Priority 2 is updating, re-signing, and disseminating the IASC Principals’Statements on PSEA and Sexual Harassment toreaffirm current IASC leaders’ strongcommitment to taking action against all formsof sexual misconduct. The Statement alsounderscores the critical role of humanitariancoordinators and humanitarian country officesin implementing PSEA measures in all responseoperations.
UPDATES
Consultations were held with the IASCTechnical Advisory Group to define theStatement priorities.
The respective IASC Principals' Statements onPSEA and Sexual Harassment were updatedand combined into one statement on PSEAH.
The Statement was endorsed by IASCPrincipals.
COMING SOON • The Statement will be launched throughan IASC video and online campaign, to beconducted in Q3 2024.
Another key initiative under Priority 2 isbuilding and expanding the work of theImplementing Partner Protocol Working Group.
UPDATES
Consultations with the UN ImplementingPartner Protocol Working Group and AdultLearning Specialists were held to informabout the gaps, challenges and prioritiesregarding the implementation of the jointUN Harmonized Implementation Tool.
An e-learning course to support the learningof NGOs, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)and UN partners on the operationalizationof the UN Implementing Partner ProtocolWorking Group and the use of the PSEAmodule in the UN Partner Portal is currentlybeing designed.
COMING SOON
The e-learning course is expected to befinalized by Q3 2024.
A global IASC “Training of Trainers”work-shop will be organized in Q32024. The work-shop will bringtogether IASC PSEA Coordinators fromselected countries and representa-tives from NGOs and CSOs engaged inthe im-plementation of the UNImplementing Partner PSEA CapacityAssessment tool.

3 Supporting Continued Capacity Strengthening Across the Sector
The key initiatives under Priority 3 are identifying and promoting good practices across the clustersystem and the Development of guidelines and resources to contribute to reducing SEA risks inhumanitarian assistance, including cash transfers. This is being achieved by working across thecluster system with cooperating partners and financial service providers to enhance andaccelerate the integration of PSEA principles and approaches into humanitarian systems.
UPDATES
Consultations were held with IASC members and Empowered Aid to support strengthenedprogrammatic responses and PSEA risk analysis.
A summary report of key priorities and agreed upon actions for the clusters was prepared andprovided to all participating cluster leads and PSEA technical leads.
COMING SOON
Instructions on how to operationalize PSEA across the cluster system will be developed.
Good practices and challenges will be collected and shared to build upon the strengths ofdifferent clusters and further enhance global work on PSEA.
The WFP Ethics Office PSEA Team and the IASC PSEAH teams conducted consultations with allcluster leads and their respective PSEA technical leads. This consultation facilitated discussionaround supporting capacity strengthening and co-designing deliverables this year to address thechallenges facing clusters when implementing PSEA across their respective organizations.
The WFP Cash Based Transfer team and WFP Ethics Office PSEA Team developed a non-mandatoryassessment to support WFP country offices in evaluating capacities of Financial Service Providersto comply with institutional PSEA standards. This tool was piloted by the WFP Afghanistan countryoffices.
A mapping of available cluster guidance will be conducted and issued to provide an overviewof how PSEA is represented across different forms of guidance, policies and handbooks.
WFP will explore opportunities with the IASC to adapt the non-mandatory assessment toolfor evaluating capacities of Financial Service Providers into an interagency tool.

Happening within WFP
For the Championship to be successful, collective commitment, full engagement and support hasbeen provided across the organization, showing that PSEAH is a collective responsibility and aninstitution-wide commitment. The following are some highlights of internal initiatives:
To kick off the Championship internally, the Executive Director sent an email to allemployees with a video outlining the priorities and calling on everyone to play their part.This was further amplified by other visibility initiatives, including a WFPGo article, socialmedia and visibility around WFP HQ, Regional and Country Offices.
The Executive Director has included PSEAH across her engagements with WFP teams – fromRegional Management Team meetings, meetings with senior leadership, all team meetings inCountry Office and any opportunity that presents itself.
Regional Directors, Deputy Regional Directors, Country Directors, and Deputy CountryDirectors were briefed on the Championship, the outlined priorities and provided withtailored guidance and messaging.
In collaboration with the Regional Bureaus, the WFP Ethics Office organized regional PSEAFocal Point workshops in the WFP Regional Bureaus for Panama and Nairobi, bringing togethertechnical PSEA focal points from the respective regional country offices. The workshops wereorganized to reinforce and continue the operationalization of WFP’s commitments on PSEA.
Country Directors participating in the Regional Management Team meetings in the RegionalBureaus in Dakar, Nairobi, and Panama received PSEA senior leader training to support themwith information to prevent incidents of SEA in the field, and to foster a culture of zerotolerance for inaction on SEA. Additional sessions for other Regional Bureaus are anticipated.
Newly appointed Country Directors and Deputy Country Directors are continuing to receivePSEA sessions through the induction training programme.
A PSEA training session was integrated into the “Safe and Secure Approaches to FieldEnvironments” (SSAFE) training hosted by the Security Division in Brindisi. The traininghighlights SEA as a serious breach of trust which can have a negative impact on safety andsecurity in the field.

The Executive Director’s Global Outreach
During her global outreach, the Executive Director is leveraging her extensive experienceand influence to drive change through the PSEAH Championship. She is dedicated tocultivating a safer and more respectful environment across the humanitarian sector byenhancing protection for victims/survivors and at-risk communities.
The Executive Director has prioritized PSEAH during her recent travels, using theopportunity to do a deep-dive into the issue and what WFP and the humanitarian system isdoing. In all of her engagements in the field, the Executive Director emphasized the criticalimportance of collective efforts to eradicate forms of SEA and sexual harassment from thehumanitarian system, and reiterated the important role that every has to play.
“We represent hope. We give dignity. We have respect. And if we don’t have respect forone another, how can we haverespect for those we serve? In allyour dealings with each other andthe communities we serve, yourepresent the finest humanitarianorganization there is. So, representit with pride and make yourbehaviors and interactions anexample.”
Executive Director McCain

The Executive Director’s Global Outreach
Some recent examples field missions include:
South Sudan
Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
Philippines
Zambia
Jordan
Antigua and Barbuda
